why_angle: The roundups in this search put the Panasonic SC-PM270 in 'AM FM' lists without saying it has no AM band. None of them explains that AM comes in through an antenna inside the case and that you aim it by turning the whole unit. This page sorts every candidate by the bands listed in its maker spec or manual, adds today's prices and says which models skip AM.

page.title: CD Player with Radio: Which Ones Get AM and FM (2026)
page.h1: CD player with radio: which ones have AM as well as FM
page.desc: CD players with radio compared on AM/FM bands, batteries, Bluetooth and discs, using maker manuals. Includes today's prices for GPX, Jensen, Sony, Panasonic and Philips.
page.answer: Short answer. The best CD player with AM FM radio for most people is the GPX BC112B boombox ($26.49): CD plus AM and FM, on 6 C batteries or AC. Jensen's CD-560 adds Bluetooth. Panasonic's SC-PM270 is FM only, 87.5–108 MHz. For AM, turn the whole unit: its AM antenna is inside the case.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Bluetooth costs $23.50 more: $49.99 (Jensen CD-560) − $26.49 (GPX BC112B) = $23.50. The CD-560's Bluetooth only receives, so it plays your phone but can't send sound to headphones.
  • Batteries: a Target up&up 8-pack of C cells is $12.99, or $1.62 a cell. The GPX takes 6 (6 × $1.62 ≈ $9.74 a set) and the Jensen CD-560 and CD-490 take 8 ($12.99 a set).
  • Sony's battery cost per hour: Sony rates the CFD-S70 at about 10 h of CD play on 6 C cells, so $9.74 ÷ 10 h ≈ $0.97 per hour.
  • Sony's price: the only US offer we could open was a refurbished unit at $159.99. $159.99 ÷ $26.49 ≈ 6× the price of the GPX.
  • Volume: Panasonic rates the SC-PM270 at 10 W + 10 W (6 Ω, 10% THD) and Sony rates the CFD-S70 at 1.7 W + 1.7 W (4 Ω, 10% THD). 20 ÷ 3.4 ≈ 5.9× the rated power, but the Panasonic must stay plugged in.

AM or FM: which antenna does the work

On these boomboxes the telescopic aerial is for FM. AM comes in through an antenna built into the case. Sony's CFD-S70 manual lists 'AM: Built-in ferrite bar antenna' and says to 'reorient the unit itself for optimum reception'. Jensen's CD-490 manual tells you to extend and rotate the telescopic antenna for FM, and for AM to hold the unit upright and move it around. GPX's BC112 manual labels its rod 'Telescopic FM Antenna'. So if AM stations are faint, turn the whole radio rather than pulling out the rod. Sony's manual also names mobile phones near the unit as a source of noise.

One Target reviewer of the Jensen CD-560 wrote that it 'doesn't pick many AM stations that my tiny portable radio can do just fine'. If you mostly listen to AM talk or sports, place it near a window and turn it for the clearest signal.

Some CD radios have no AM band at all. Panasonic's own North American spec for the SC-PM270 lists only FM (87.5–108 MHz, 30 presets) and 120 V AC power. Target's listing for the Philips TAZ4300 describes FM with 30 presets and doesn't mention AM. Philips' TAZ6000/10 leaflet lists DAB+/FM radio. If you want AM, buy one of the GPX, Jensen or Sony models. If FM at home is all you need, the {buy:panasonic-sc-pm270} is the loudest unit here.

Not recommended

Jensen CD-490 at today's Target price. At $62.99 from a third-party seller it costs $62.99 − $49.99 = $13.00 more than the Jensen CD-560. It takes the same 8 C cells, Target lists no Bluetooth, and Jensen's manual rules out computer CDs, so burned MP3 discs won't play.
